newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas called higher with power prices.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas called higher with power prices.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures were expected to open marginally higher Wednesday ahead of American Gas Association's storage data, market sources said.
"It's the screaming electricity market," one trader said, adding he heard next-day peak prices into Cinergy (East Central Area Reliability Coordination Agreement) as high as $325 per megawatt hour.
August over-the-counter trade ranged from $2.17 to $2.18 after settling to the upside Tuesday at $2.162 per million British thermal units.
On ACCESS, August remained in a tight range, last trading 0.3 cent higher at $2.165.

Triggering the frenzied electricity market and marginal climb in the natgas market have been above-normal temperatures across most of the U.S., with highs near 100 degrees F in parts of the Northeast, Midwest and Gulf Coast.
Chart traders said August resistance was still along the down trendline at $2.23. Support was seen at last week's $2.051 low, with psychological buying at $2.

In Tuesday's cash, Gulf Coast gas firmed three cents to the high-teens. Midcon pipes were four cents higher around $2.10, while New York city gate prices jumped another five cents to the low-to-mid $2.50s.
Early Wednesday cash prices at the Henry Hub were talked a bit higher at $2.21-2.23 per mmBtu.
Injection estimates for the storage report range from 78 bcf to 101 bcf. For the same week last year, stocks gained 94 bcf.
